[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (2C) If a person sends a paper form or document to the court using an address that is not the relevant OCMC postal address or relevant OCMC email address, the court may send it to the relevant OCMC postal address or relevant OCMC email address. (The form or document is still treated as submitted to the court when it was received at the first address.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] 14.1(3) If a time limit imposed by or set in accordance with this practice direction or in directions expires on a day when the CTSC (as defined) is closed, a form, document or email is still submitted on time if it is submitted before 4.00 p.m. on the next day the court office is open. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (Civil Procedure Rule Practice Direction 2A paragraph 3.2 sets out the days when court offices (including the CTSC) are closed.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] Submitting documents at court– responsibility for submitting documents on time

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] 14.1A(1) Where any time limit applies (whether imposed by this practice direction or in any other way) it is the relevant party’s responsibility to ensure that a form, document or email is submitted on time , subject to sub-paragraph (2). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (2) If –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (a) a party correctly and within any relevant time limit attempts to upload a form or document, including information required by an order, rule or practice direction (“a submission”);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (b) the upload of the submission is unsuccessful solely as a result of the OCMC website not permitting the submission to be uploaded at that time;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (c) the party, as soon as practicable upon being notified of this by the OCMC website, correctly repeats the step of uploading the submission until it is then confirmed as completed by the OCMC website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (d) successful upload occurs after the relevant time limit has expired, the party is to be treated as having uploaded the submission on time. ## Documents scanned by the bulk scanning provider – treated as true copy of the original by the court

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Documents scanned by the bulk scanning provider – treated as true copy of the original by the court] 14.2 The court will treat a scan of a document from the bulk scanning provider electronically transmitted to HMCTS’s secure digital platform as a true copy of the original document. ## Changes to Practice Direction 32 – Evidence

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Changes to Practice Direction 32 – Evidence] 14.3 (1) In relation to claims that are started using Online Civil Money Claims, the Civil Procedure Rules Practice Direction 32 (Evidence) is changed as set out in subparagraph (2). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Changes to Practice Direction 32 – Evidence] (2) In Practice Direction 32, for paragraph 27.6, substitute—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Changes to Practice Direction 32 – Evidence] 27.6(1) Subject to sub-paragraph (2), the originals of the documents contained in the trial bundle, together with copies of any other court orders should be available at the trial. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Changes to Practice Direction 32 – Evidence] (2)  Where a claim is started using Online Civil Money Claims in accordance with Practice Direction 51R, the court will treat a scan of a document from the bulk scanning provider electronically transmitted to HM Courts and Tribunal Service’s secure digital platform with an identity number as a true copy of the original document. The original need not be made available at the trial. (“Bulk scanning provider” has the meaning given in Practice Direction 51R.)

## Evidence and other documents to be filed at court

## 14.4(1) Sub-paragraph (2) applies where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.4(1) Sub-paragraph (2) applies where –] (a) the parties are represented;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.4(1) Sub-paragraph (2) applies where –] (b) the all parties are unrepresented or one of the parties is represented by a legal representative. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.4(1) Sub-paragraph (2) applies where –] (2) Unless the document cannot be uploaded to the OCMC website, any document which a party wishes to file or is required to file at court must be uploaded to the OCMC website, and must be in one of the machine-readable formats accepted by the OCMC website. (Paragraph 2.1(2) and (2A) sets out how documents that cannot be uploaded to the OCMC website may be submitted to the court instead.)

## SECTION 15 – FORM OF JUDGMENTS – STANDARD REQUIREMENTS

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 15 – FORM OF JUDGMENTS – STANDARD REQUIREMENTS] Form of judgments – standard requirements

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 15 – FORM OF JUDGMENTS – STANDARD REQUIREMENTS] 15.1(1) Any judgment, order or “directions” (as defined) made under this practice direction must state the name and the judicial title or other official role of the person who made them. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 15 – FORM OF JUDGMENTS – STANDARD REQUIREMENTS] (2) A party must comply with a judgment or order for the payment of money (including costs) within 19 days of the date of the judgment or order, unless –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 15 – FORM OF JUDGMENTS – STANDARD REQUIREMENTS] (a) the judgment or order sets a different date for the payment;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 15 – FORM OF JUDGMENTS – STANDARD REQUIREMENTS] (b) any of the provisions of this practice direction specifies a different time for compliance; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 15 – FORM OF JUDGMENTS – STANDARD REQUIREMENTS] (c) the court has “stayed” (as defined) the proceedings or judgment. ## SECTION 16 – PROCESS FOR RESUMING A CLAIM THAT HAS BEEN STAYED (“LIFTING” A STAY)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 16 – PROCESS FOR RESUMING A CLAIM THAT HAS BEEN STAYED (“LIFTING” A STAY)] Process for resuming a claim that has been stayed (“lifting” a stay)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 16 – PROCESS FOR RESUMING A CLAIM THAT HAS BEEN STAYED (“LIFTING” A STAY)] 16.1(1) This Section sets out the process for lifting a stay of proceedings (as defined) so that proceedings on a claim may be resumed. If, however, another provision contains provisions about resuming claims that have been stayed in particular circumstances, that provision prevails to the extent that it is inconsistent with this Section. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 16 – PROCESS FOR RESUMING A CLAIM THAT HAS BEEN STAYED (“LIFTING” A STAY)] (2) If the proceedings have been stayed and all the parties are acting in person, any party may make an application to the court to “lift” the stay (as defined) so that the proceedings on the claim can be resumed. (Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 16 – PROCESS FOR RESUMING A CLAIM THAT HAS BEEN STAYED (“LIFTING” A STAY)] (3) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 16 – PROCESS FOR RESUMING A CLAIM THAT HAS BEEN STAYED (“LIFTING” A STAY)] (4) If the court receives an application to lift the stay, the court must refer the application to a judge for directions, which may include that the claim be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims. ## SECTION 16A – COURT MAY REFER MATTERS TO A JUDGE OR LEGAL ADVISER

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 16A – COURT MAY REFER MATTERS TO A JUDGE OR LEGAL ADVISER] Court may refer matters to a judge or legal adviser

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 16A – COURT MAY REFER MATTERS TO A JUDGE OR LEGAL ADVISER] 16A.1 At any time, the court may refer any matter relating to a claim to a judge or a “legal adviser” (as defined) if appropriate for an order, or directions as to how the claim or matter is to be handled. The directions may include that the claim be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims. It will only be appropriate for a legal adviser to consider a particular matter if a provision elsewhere in the Civil Procedure Rules enables them to consider matters of that type. ## SECTION 16B – APPLICATIONS

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 16B – APPLICATIONS] A pplications for court orders – online applications

## 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (2) Subject to subparagraph (10)-

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (a) a represented party wishing to make an application must make an online application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (b) a party acting in person wishing to make an application may make an online application. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (3) The applicant makes an online application using the OCMC website by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (a) completing the relevant screens on the website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (b) submitting the online application to the court using the website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (4) An online application is to be treated as the application notice for the purposes of the Civil Procedure Rules and in particular Part 23. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (5) Unless the online application is made without notice under Civil Procedure Rule 23.4, the respondent is to be notified, through the OCMC website, of the application as soon as it is made. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (6) If the applicant requests that the online application is made without notice to the respondent, the application is to be referred to a judge to consider the request, or referred to a legal adviser for the legal adviser to consider the request, if it would be appropriate for the legal adviser to do so. It will only be appropriate for a legal adviser to consider a request if a provision elsewhere in the Civil Procedure Rules enables them to consider requests of this type. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (7) After an online application has been made and unless the application is to be dealt with without notice, the respondent must provide initial information to assist with managing the future conduct of the application (“respondent information”) by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (a) completing the relevant screens on the OCMC website;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (b) submitting the completed screens to the court using the website;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (c) if relevant and requested to do so by the court, confirming whether the respondent consents to the application. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (8) If the respondent confirms that they had consented to the application and that their consent was given before the application was made, the application is to be treated as an application for a consent order and the requirements in rule 40.6(7)(c) and PD 40B paragraph 3.4(3) are disapplied. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (9) The respondent must provide their respondent information –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (a) before 4pm on the 5 th day after the date of notification of the online application; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (b) within such other time limit notified to the respondent at the same time that the respondent is notified of the online application as directed by the Designated Civil Judge Online. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (10) In addition to any applications that are required to be made as on-paper applications under paragraph 7.45, the following applications must also be made as on-paper applications –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (a) any application made before a claim has been issued;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (b) any application for default judgment under paragraph 11.1B(8) where there is a Mental Health Crisis Moratorium in place under the Debt Respite Scheme (Breathing Space Moratorium and Mental Health Crisis Moratorium) (England and Wales) Regulations 2020 ;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (ba) any application for the determination of the amount of costs or disbursements under Civil Procedure Rule 45.64 (determination  where all parties agree on all issues except costs);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (c) any application relating to—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (i) an appeal;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (ii) enforcement; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (iii) insolvency; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (d) any application where any respondent is not already a party to the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] O ther applications

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] 16B.2 (1) If a party wishes to make an application that is not an online application or otherwise covered by a provision of this practice direction, the application must be made using the procedure set out in the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] (2) Any application made under subparagraph (1) is to be made to the CTSC or, where the parties have received an order from a judge or “legal adviser”(as defined) at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, that hearing centre. When the court receives any such application, the application must be considered by a judge or a “legal adviser” (as defined), if appropriate, who must give directions as to how the application is to be handled. The directions may include a direction that the claim is to be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims, unless the application is an application for the determination of costs or disbursements under Civil Procedure Rule 45.64, in which the case the directions must include that the claim be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] Procedure where the parties make a request to the court not covered by online civil money claims

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 16B.1(1) This paragraph applies where a party wishes to make an application.] 17.1(1) If the claimant or defendant wants to make a request to the court which is not catered for by this practice direction but is permitted by a provision elsewhere in the Civil Procedure Rules or Practice Directions, or by a court order, that party must notify the CTSC or, where the parties have received an order from a judge or a “legal adviser” (as defined) at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, that hearing centre. ## SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS] The claimant or defendant no longer wishes to take part in the Online Civil Money Claims

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS] 18.1 If the claimant or defendant no longer wishes to take part in Online Civil Money Claims, they may request that the court sends the claim out. If the court receives such a request, it must refer the matter to a judge. The judge must then direct that the claim be sent out of the Online Civil Money Claims. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS] Court considers that a claim is not – or is no longer – suitable for Online Civil Money Claims

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS] 18.2(1) Where a claim has not already been transferred out of Online Civil Money Claims but the court, at any stage, concludes that the claim is not suitable for Online Civil Money Claims, or is no longer suitable for it, or is otherwise not appropriate for it –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS] (a) the court must transfer the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims, if the reason that the claim is not, or is no longer, suitable or appropriate for the pilot is that a party wishes to take a step in proceedings not catered for by the pilot; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS] (b) a judge must transfer the claim out. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS] (2) When the court transfers a claim out of Online Civil Money Claims under paragraph (1)(a), the court must transfer the claim to the CNBC unless the claim had already been transferred to a County Court hearing centre, in which case the court must transfer the claim out of the pilot to that hearing centre. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 18 – PARTIES OR THE COURT REQUIRING THE CLAIM TO BE SENT OUT OF ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS] Process for sending a claim out of online civil money claims where no other provision applies

## 19.1(1). If –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 19.1(1). If –] (a) a provision of this practice direction requires the court or a judge to send a claim out of Online Civil Money Claims; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 19.1(1). If –] (b) under “directions” (as defined) a claim is to be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims,  then this Section sets out the process for sending the claim out. If, however, another provision applies to a particular claim and sets out the whole or part of the process for sending out, that provision prevails to the extent that it is inconsistent with this Section. ## 19.1(2) A judge must decide where to send a claim that is being sent out. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 19.1(2) A judge must decide where to send a claim that is being sent out.] 19.1(3) To ensure that a claim is sent out of Online Civil Money Claims successfully, the court may give directions (as defined) about how the claim is to be sent out.The court may also give directions about the future management of the claim. Directions given under this paragraph may include directions changing how any of the Civil Procedure Rules or any of the other practice directions will apply to the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 19.1(2) A judge must decide where to send a claim that is being sent out.] 19.1(4) If the court sends a claim out of Online Civil Money Claims, the court must inform the claimant and defendant of this and must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 19.1(2) A judge must decide where to send a claim that is being sent out.] (a) explain why the claim has been sent out; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 19.1(2) A judge must decide where to send a claim that is being sent out.] (b) set out any directions given by the court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 19.1(2) A judge must decide where to send a claim that is being sent out.] 19.1(5) Once the court sends the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims, this practice direction will no longer apply to the claim, but the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules and other practice directions will continue to apply, with any changes that the court has directed and with the following modifications: any of the party’s form N180, N181 or online directions questionnaires is treated as that party’s completed directions questionnaire form N180 or N181 as appropriate, completed under Civil Procedure Rules Part 26. ## SECTION 20 – LEGAL ADVISERS

## Scope of this Section

## 20.1(1) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 20.1(1) Omitted] (2) This Section sets out what court powers (jurisdiction) a “legal adviser” (as defined) can use in relation to a claim in Online Civil Money Claims, and the limits on using those powers. It also sets out what action a party can take if they are unhappy with anything done by a legal adviser. (The definition of a legal adviser is set out in paragraph 1.1 of this Practice Direction. In brief, a legal adviser is a member of court staff who is a barrister, solicitor or Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Legal Executives or a CILEX lawyer, who has been authorised to act as a legal adviser by relevant judges.)

## Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] 20.2(1) A legal adviser may exercise the jurisdiction of the county court in relation to all the powers that are set out in the first column of Table A that is set out in the Schedule to this Section. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (2) Legal advisers may only exercise a particular power in so far as it is not limited by anything in the second column of that Table A, or by any of the general limits on the exercise of powers set out in paragraph (3) below. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (3) The general limits on legal advisers exercising any power are that –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (a) a legal adviser must not make a final decision on any claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (b) a legal adviser must not exercise any power in relation to a claim where the defendant’s response is submitted to the court on paper rather than electronically except where the response is a defence of the whole of the claim and paragraph 10.3 applies;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (c) if a legal adviser considers that a claim requires a hearing in advance of a trial, the legal adviser must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (d) if a claim is complicated, the legal adviser must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the “preferred court” (as defined); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (e) a legal adviser must not send a claim out of the pilot until the later of–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (i) the end of the time for a party to request reconsideration by a judge of the legal adviser’s decision (see paragraph 20.3(2A) and (3)); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (ii) the determination of any reconsideration. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (4) A claim is complicated and must be sent out of the pilot if –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (a) the claim raises a substantial point of law;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (b) the claim has a complicated factual background; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (c) more than one expert per claim is to provide an opinion. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Jurisdiction of legal advisers – and limits on the jurisdiction] (5) A legal adviser may consider a claim to be complicated for any other reason, and if so the legal adviser must still send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the “preferred court” (as defined). ## Reconsideration of a decision made by a legal adviser

## 20.3(1) Decisions of a legal adviser will be made without a hearing. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 20.3(1) Decisions of a legal adviser will be made without a hearing.] (2) A party may request any decision of a legal adviser to be reconsidered by a judge, and any request must be made on time. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 20.3(1) Decisions of a legal adviser will be made without a hearing.] (2A) If the legal adviser’s decision related to a claim where the defendant’s response–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 20.3(1) Decisions of a legal adviser will be made without a hearing.] (a) was submitted on paper,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 20.3(1) Decisions of a legal adviser will be made without a hearing.] (b) is a defence of the whole of the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 20.3(1) Decisions of a legal adviser will be made without a hearing.] (c) and paragraph 10.3 applies,
